claims.claim: ⚠️ **Systemic hypocalcaemia can follow skin exposure alone.** Pain can come late and be out of proportion to what is visible.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not use local anaesthetic techniques for pain** — they can mask ongoing symptoms.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HF is corrosive; whatever the route, it is toxic systemically via fluorosis, which shows as hypocalcaemia.** Sources: rust cleaners, car wheel cleaners (aluminium brightener), glass etching, industry. Concentrations run up to 70%; domestic products are likely under 5%.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **All exposures need medical assessment.** ⚠️ **Hypocalcaemia risk:** over 1% BSA with over 50% HF · over 5% BSA at any concentration · **any ingestion.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fluorosis (any route) → hypocalcaemia and hypomagnesaemia:** perioral numbness, paraesthesiae, cramps · irritability, seizures · tetany · Chovostek's and Trosseau's signs · ⚠️ arrhythmias (long QT) · heart failure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Skin pain is immediate with over 50% HF but can be delayed up to 24 hours with weaker solutions**, and may precede any blistering or erythema as a marker of tissue destruction.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ingestion:** under 20% irritates the oesophagus; higher concentrations may burn. **Inhalation:** immediate irritation, but cough, wheeze and breathlessness may be delayed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Investigations:** electrolytes and blood gas (calcium, magnesium, potassium) · **ECG — prolonged QT marks hypocalcaemia** · consider urgent endoscopy after ingestion.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Put calcium gluconate 2.5% gel on the contaminated skin, reapplying every 15 minutes until the pain stops.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No gel available?** Make one by adding 10 mL of calcium gluconate 10% injection to 30 mL of sterile surgical lubricant.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Remove clothing and jewellery into sealed bags out of patient areas; wash off, scrubbing under nails.** ⚠️ **Staff wear PPE including chemical-resistant gloves.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eyes: flush with 0.9% saline.** ⚠️ **Ingestion: no activated charcoal — it is not indicated.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Everyone at risk of fluorosis — including all ingestions — is managed in a resuscitation area on continuous cardiac monitoring.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cardiac arrest or ventricular arrhythmia: calcium gluconate 10% 0.5 mL/kg, max 60 mL** — higher than the standard maximum.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Plus IV sodium bicarbonate 1 mmol/kg, i.e. 1 mL/kg of the 1 mmol/mL solution.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Plus magnesium sulfate IV, as the 50% (2 mmol/mL) solution:** VF **0.1–0.2 mmol/kg (= 0.05–0.1 mL/kg), given slowly IV**; deficiency **0.4 mmol/kg (= 0.2 mL/kg) over 4 hours.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Correct hypocalcaemia with calcium gluconate 10% 0.5 mL/kg**; repeated and higher doses may be needed — discuss with a toxicologist. Correct other electrolytes too.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Skin:** calcium gluconate 2.5% gel topically, repeated every 15 minutes. **Inhalation: nebulise calcium gluconate 10%, 1 mL diluted in 3 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refractory pain:** discuss with Poisons Information (131126) — subcutaneous calcium gluconate 0.5 mL/cm², regional IV or intra-arterial infusion. ⚠️ **Calcium chloride damages tissue, so never infiltrate it locally or regionally.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A child at risk of systemic fluorosis needs 12 hours of monitoring.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider admission for all adolescents with intentional exposure**; assess self-harm risk before ward transfer, but **never delay urgent care such as ICU admission.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Transfer** if care is beyond the local hospital's comfort. **PIPER: 1300 137 650.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge:** simple analgesia alone controls the pain · GCS normal · normal ECG (if required) · observation period complete · after deliberate ingestion, low assessed risk of further self-harm.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Hydrofluoric acid exposure' (Last Updated October 2018), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_acid_exposure/, retrieved 2026-09-23
